newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish conservative hints at October polls.
newsitem.headline: Turkish conservative hints at October polls.

text.p: A conservative Turkish minister said on Saturday polls could be held as early as October as a way of overcoming the political crisis now gripping the Islamist-led coalition.
"We do not know the certain date but elections could take place in mid-October," state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Health Minister Ismail Karakuyu as saying.
"Elections will diminish the tension in the country," Karakuyu said.

The minister's secularist True Path Party has been locked in tough bargaining with its Islamist coalition partners over a possible date for early elections in a last-ditch effort to save their 11-month-old government from collapse.

True Path leader Tansu Ciller has promised her party she would press Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, to let her lead the country to polls as caretaker head of government.
However, the two sides have so far been unable to agree on a date. Turkish press reports say Erbakan was pushing for a quick poll, but Ciller was holding out for a date sometime next spring.
Elections would normally be due by the year 2000.
The talks have taken on greater urgency with the resignation on Friday of a senior conservative MP, stripping the coalition of an absolute majority in parliament.
That leaves Erbakan clinging to just 275 seats in the 550-member parliament, one short of the majority needed to win a confidence vote. Two seats are vacant.
Under the existing coalition protocol, Ciller was to take over the prime minister's office in June of 1998.
However, Karakuyu said other provisions of the agreement stipulated that the True Path would head the government in the event of early polls.
"When the election is on Turkey's agenda, the prime minister's office must be handed to (True Path) leader Tansu Ciller according to the coalition protocol," he said.
